transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-31
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Nair (Redwood); Jonah Rivera, Lisa Park, Omar Haddad, Katrina Wu (Catalyst)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/production-playbook (deck), s3://catalyst-samples/llm-prompts (note)

Summary:
Catalyst Analytics is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployment. Primary drivers: long-context summarization of streaming telemetry (32k -> 128k in spikes), Spanish/Portuguese multilingual support for LATAM customers, and tool-calling to hit internal APIs (DB lookup + enrichment). Security team flagged KMS + audit log requirements; Ops team cares about latency SLAs for near-real-time alerts (~200-400ms p95 for short queries, higher tolerated for batch summarization).

Topics covered:
- Model families and open model tradeoffs (Mistral / Llama / Falcon variants, RedPajama forks)
- Context window needs and cost implications (32k vs 128k windows, KV cache impact)
- Tool-calling and structured outputs (function calling, tool-routing)
- Deployment modes: Hosted API for initial pilot, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, data residency

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for doing this — we'll kick off, quick intros. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, Diego is our SE, Priya is a solutions engineer.
[00:12] Jonah Rivera: hey, Jonah here — CTO at Catalyst. We're trying to scope where an LLM layer sits in our stack, um and what deployment mode makes sense.
[00:20] Lisa Park: Lisa — ML eng. primary workload is continuous telemetry summarization and answer retrieval from an internal knowledge base.
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: nice. can you say a little about the context lengths you're seeing? is it mostly short queries or long docs?
[00:34] Lisa Park: mostly long, so like 20k tokens at times, spikes to 80-120k when we stitch 24h of logs for incident retrospectives. we don't need real-time for the big retros, but the summarization should be accurate.
[00:47] Maya Chen: okay so two classes — streaming/near-real-time (shorter context) and heavy retros (very long). On Redwood we typically recommend different model + routing strategies for each; also KV cache and prefix caching can dramatically reduce cost for repeated sequences.
[01:05] Jonah Rivera: when you say "different model" do you mean smaller quantized models for short queries and large context ones for retros? is that switch automatic?
[01:12] Priya Nair: yeah — we often run a lower-latency quantized 7-10B for short Q/A, then route to a 30-70B 32k/128k variant for long-form generation. routing can be policy-based (latency budget, cost budget, region). there is also automatic fallback if capacity is constrained.
[01:30] Lisa Park: what about open models — we looked at Mistral 7B/40B, Llama 2 derivatives, RedPajama/Instruct, and some commercial ones. Any guidance which are production ready?
[01:40] Diego Alvarez: good question. Mistral-40B variants give strong generation quality and perform well with quantization for cost, but context window support varies; some community forks extend to 32k. Llama derivatives are stable and well-supported but licensing sometimes messy. Redwood maintains a performance profile per model; we can share our 32k perf bench for Catalyst-like inputs.
[02:03] Jonah Rivera: licensing is a big factor for us — we can't ship models with restrictive terms across clients in LATAM.
[02:09] Maya Chen: understood — we'll attach the model licensing summary. for private deployments we can pin validated model binaries to your environment which helps legal.
[02:18] Omar Haddad: security note — we need KMS integration, bring-your-own-key, and full audit logs exportable to our SIEM. Also we have to meet an equivalent of HIPAA controls for certain customers. can Redwood support hardware HSMs?
[02:33] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. for Hosted we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS and can stream audit logs. for Dedicated and Private we can arrange HSM-backed key stores. there are some setup steps for on-prem.
[02:50] Katrina Wu: regarding multilingual: we need Spanish/Portuguese as first-class — will quality degrade for these models?
[02:57] Diego Alvarez: Depends on model family and fine-tuning. Mistral-40B variants tend to be okay in Romance languages; some Llama-based models trained on diverse corpora show stronger multilinguality. We also recommend targeted fine-tuning or instruction tuning on in-domain multilingual data. Redwood Optimize includes guidance on quantization and fine-tune suggestions.
[03:18] Jonah Rivera: and tool-calling — we want the model to call internal enrichment APIs (customer lookup, anonymization). how do you secure tool-calls?
[03:25] Priya Nair: function-calling is supported. we recommend a proxy layer in your VPC that validates function calls, enforces RBAC, and strips PHI before calling downstream. For Hosted, we can provide secure tool-call proxies and signed tokens; for Private, calls stay inside your network.
[03:44] Lisa Park: any real numbers on latency for tool calls — our alerting path needs sub-400ms p95 for short queries that trigger DB hit + enrichment.
[03:53] Diego Alvarez: for small models on Dedicated with colocated DBs you can hit 150-300ms p95 for the model step; tool-call add depends on your network and proxy. we can run a quick estimator given your expected QPS and average response sizes.
[04:08] Jonah Rivera: cost — what's the delta between hosted vs dedicated vs private for our expected throughput?
[04:15] Maya Chen: hosted is easiest to start — pay-as-you-go, slightly higher per-token unit cost but no infra ops. Dedicated gives committed-price throughput, helps predict unit economics. Private has platform fee + infra ops but best for strict compliance and data residency. we'll send a side-by-side with rough TCO for 3 use patterns (pilot, steady state, and peak retros).
[04:35] Omar Haddad: does Redwood provide multi-region routing? we have customers in Brazil and Mexico and want lower latency for those regions.
[04:41] Priya Nair: yes, smart routing by region with policy rules. for strict data residency we can route requests to specific regions or keep them in your VPC.
[04:50] Lisa Park: any gotchas for KV cache — will it blow up memory on 128k sequences?
[04:55] Diego Alvarez: KV cache growth is linear with tokens. for 128k windows we recommend chunking and streaming summarization. Redwood runtime supports compressed KV cache and eviction policies; also you can offload cache to fast NVMe with modest perf hit.
[05:12] Jonah Rivera: okay let's talk POC — timeline and success metrics. we want: 1) accurate 24h incident summarization (ROUGE/QA pass rate), 2) <400ms p95 for short enrichment calls, 3) bilingual quality parity (es/pt).
[05:27] Maya Chen: great, propose a 6-week POC: week 1—data & security intake, week 2—baseline model selection + perf bench, weeks 3-4—integration and tool-calling test, week 5—user acceptance tests, week 6—wrap & ops handoff.
[05:40] Katrina Wu: who needs to be involved from Redwood for the infra work?
[05:44] Priya Nair: Diego will lead the bench and integration, Priya will help with security and deployment design, Maya will handle commercial/contract. We'll also pull in our infra specialists for the Private install if you go that route.
[05:56] Lisa Park: will you share a sample bench script? we can run local probes against our staging data.
[06:00] Diego Alvarez: yes — we'll share the benchmark harness and a quick-start config.
[06:05] Jonah Rivera: one last thing — we've got an existing in-house ensembling layer that shards prompts across models for cost/perf; can Redwood's smart routing plug into that?
[06:14] Priya Nair: absolutely — we have routing APIs and webhook-based decision hooks so your ensembling layer can call Redwood or Redwood can call your router. it's flexible.
[06:24] Maya Chen: cool. recap on next steps: we'll send model perf + licensing summary, tailored pricing/POC plan, bench harness, and security docs. Catalyst to send sample prompts + compliance checklist.
[06:36] Jonah Rivera: perfect — Omar will send the security checklist. Lisa will get prompt samples.
[06:40] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for POC kickoff.
[06:45] Lisa Park: thanks everyone.
[06:47] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of model names and product nouns, some speaker overlap at times, timestamps approximate.
